model.rationale: A twelve-point Democratic lean, Tokuda's incumbency, and a roughly seven-to-one fundraising edge over Brenton Awa all point to a comfortable re-election, and prediction markets agree at about 94% Democratic. With no polls available, the forecast rests on those fundamentals, which leave little doubt about the outcome.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Awa near forty percent, or a surge of outside spending on his behalf, would be the main signal that this race is tightening.

overview:
Jill Tokuda seeks a second term in a Hawaii district that leans Democratic by about twelve points. She has raised more than $820,000 and holds over $570,000 on hand, while Republican Brenton Awa has raised about $123,000 with $16,000 available. Two independents with no reported fundraising also appear on the ballot. No public general-election polls exist, and no expert raters list the race.

Prediction markets put Democratic chances near 94%, and the fundamentals point the same way: the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage all favor Tokuda. Republican candidates have historically struggled to compete in Hawaii's federal races, and Awa's limited resources reinforce that pattern. The seat remains safely in Democratic hands.
